subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the distance between a node and succeeding antinode?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: nodes sit at x = 0, λ/2, λ … and antinodes at x = λ/4, 3λ/4 …, so adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart and a node to the next antinode is λ/4. The book prints 'succeding' in the question; the spelling is corrected here.

recall_prompt: Say how nodes and antinodes are spaced in a stationary wave, and the distance from a node to the next antinode.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: How they are spaced
lines: In a stationary wave, nodes and antinodes
alternate. Two neighbouring nodes are λ/2
apart, and an antinode sits midway
steps.margin_note: First mark. State the pattern — the λ/4 answer follows from it instead of being memorised.
steps.why: Nodes fall where sin kx = 0 (x = 0, λ/2, λ …) and antinodes where sin kx = ±1 (x = λ/4, 3λ/4 …) — the antinode is exactly midway between two nodes, so the spacing pattern fixes every distance in the wave.
common_mistakes: Taking the node-to-node distance as λ — one full wavelength holds TWO loops; adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart.
Placing the antinode anywhere between the nodes — it is exactly midway.

recall.must_convey: That nodes are λ/2 apart and an antinode sits midway between two neighbouring nodes.
accept: nodes are half a wavelength apart
antinode is midway between two nodes
reject: the distance is lambda by four

steps.memory_tip: One loop = node to node = λ/2. The antinode is the middle of the loop.

steps.label: The distance
lines: So the distance from a node to the next
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Half of the λ/2 loop — write λ/4 and box it.
steps.why: The antinode is midway along the λ/2 loop, so the node-to-antinode distance is half of λ/2, which is λ/4.
common_mistakes: Writing λ/2 — that is node to NODE. Node to the next ANTINODE is λ/4.

recall.must_convey: That the distance between a node and the next antinode is λ/4.
reject: nodes are half a wavelength apart

steps.memory_tip: Node–antinode–node fits in one loop of λ/2, so each hop is λ/4.

insider_note: λ/4 is the answer, but writing the spacing pattern first is what protects the mark when the examiner asks node-to-node in another year.
